title: Petra and the Terminal
premise: Elodie Underhill has spent eleven years alone on the terraforming station Petra, tending a garden seeded for colonists who never came and maintaining a beacon whose original purpose was lost to bureaucratic erasure. When a ship that was decommissioned before launch appears in orbit carrying one passenger — a courier with Elodie's own name on the manifest, dated forty years in the future — they discover the beacon is a memory vault holding proof of who actually started the war between Earth and the Outer Colonies. The message inside could end the war, but both sides have sent hunters to destroy it, and opening the vault will erase the garden's genetic archive forever. Elodie must choose between the future they were promised and the truth that makes any future worth having, delivering the message at the cost of everything they've grown.
about_author: H. M. Hartwell is the pen name of a former orbital agriculture consultant who spent six years designing closed-loop ecosystems for stations that were ultimately never crewed. They write science fiction about people who maintain things nobody remembers wanting.

chapters.title: The Garden for No One
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A day in the rhythm of Petra: pruning, calibrating the beacon, recording logs no one answers. We learn the garden is meant for colonists who never arrived, and Elodie stays out of stubbornness more than duty. The emotional beat is quiet loneliness transformed into devotion — until the beacon pings an approach vector that shouldn't exist.

chapters.title: Manifest of the Never-Flown
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The ship Halcyon docks — decommissioned pre-launch four decades ago, its registry scrubbed. Its sole passenger is unconscious, and the manifest lists a courier named E. Underhill with a departure date forty years hence. Elodie's hands shake as they match their own signature. Emotional beat: uncanny dread braided with a terrible, thrilling recognition.

chapters.title: What the Passenger Carried
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins: the passenger, Sefa Iqbal, wakes with fragmented memories of a war already over — or not yet begun. She carries a key that fits nothing on Petra except the beacon's sealed core. Flashbacks reveal she was sent by someone who knew Elodie would be here. Emotional beat: two strangers circling a shared secret neither fully understands.

chapters.title: Hunters in the Dark
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. A Colonial interdiction vessel enters the system, broadcasting demands. Sefa reveals the beacon isn't a beacon: it's a vault of uncorrupted records from the war's first hours, proving Earth fired first — or did it? Her own memories are edited, and she can't trust which side she serves. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening into reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Rootstock
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. While Sefa sleeps, Elodie works the garden and confronts what opening the vault means: the core's memory lattice is interwoven with the seed archive. Truth or garden, not both. A quiet chapter of tending plants and weighing inheritance — what we owe the unborn versus what we owe the dead. Emotional beat: grief arriving ahead of loss.

chapters.title: The Interdiction
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The Colonial vessel boards under pretense of quarantine; its commander, Adeyemi, recognizes Sefa and claims to be her former handler. He offers Elodie amnesty and a colony berth — the future the garden was built for — if they surrender the core intact and sealed. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as rescue, and Elodie realizing everyone wants the message buried.

chapters.title: Forty Years Forward
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Decoding the manifest's timestamp, they find a hidden log from the future-Elodie: a warning that the vault was opened once, the message delivered, and the war continued anyway — because it was delivered too late, after both sides had committed. The only chance is now, mid-war, when belief can still change. Emotional beat: despair transmuted into urgency.

chapters.title: Siege of the Greenhouse
chapters.summary: Split POV. Adeyemi takes the station by force; Sefa's edited memories fracture and she remembers choosing this mission freely, betraying her own side to do it. Elodie floods the greenhouse corridors with pollen and steam to cover their run to the beacon core. Emotional beat: chaos, sacrifice, and the garden itself becoming a weapon of protection.

chapters.title: The Message
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, climax. At the core, Elodie broadcasts the vault's raw record system-wide — unedited, unclaimed, addressed to no faction. The seed archive burns out as the lattice converts to signal. Adeyemi hesitates at the airlock, hearing his own younger self in the recordings. Emotional beat: terrible clarity; the cost paid without flinching, the truth loose in the dark.

chapters.title: First Planting
chapters.summary: Shared POV, resolution. Ceasefire talks begin on Petra's stripped, empty terraces — neutral ground made sacred by what it gave up. Sefa stays to testify; Elodie, archive gone, plants the last physical seed by hand. Whether peace holds is unwritten, but the message landed while anyone could still listen. Emotional beat: mourning and hope in the same handful of soil.
